about: The witch: flight in both modes, her stack, blink, spells, health and knockout.

acceleration.what: how quickly she reaches her speed or stops in the treetops (per second; higher is snappier).

treetop.what: Treetop flight: a high top speed with momentum, building a boost while she holds a direction.
treetop.notes: Treetop flight (Ed: a high top speed and momentum; the ground stays snappy): pressing a direction reaches treetopSpeed in about 0.3 s (acceleration); holding it within boostAngle degrees builds boost over boostTime seconds, up to boost times treetopSpeed; her heading turns toward the input at turnRateSlow degrees a second below sharpTurnSpeed of cruise, falling to turnRate at cruise (half that at full boost), so the size of her swoop grows with her speed (Ed); a turn of 90 degrees or more bleeds boost sharpTurnBleed times a second, and above brakeAt of cruise she skids in the brake pose; letting go, she glides to a stop over about glideTime seconds.

treetop.cameraPull.what: how far the camera draws back at full boost (a share of its distance).

leanAt.what: the share of the top speed above which she leans into her flight.

facing.what: When she and the creatures turn away from the viewer, only when clearly heading up the screen.
facing.notes: she (and every creature) faces the viewer unless clearly heading up the screen, within awayEnter degrees of straight up (and stays turned away until past awayLeave); sideways, down or stopped faces the viewer. Within headingEnter degrees of straight up or straight down the screen (until past headingLeave) she flies in her heading sprites: seen from behind going up, coming at us going down.

riseCooldown.what: After she lands she can't rise again for this many seconds [1]. 0: no wait.

decisions.rest: players rose to the treetops instead of dodging, since rising takes her out of ground mode, and out of reach, at once

cooldown.what: One shared cooldown for her dodge and her take-off.

decisions.quote: One trail, one cooldown. The trail she leaves in the treetops, landing and taking off should also appear when she dodges. Its length shows one shared cooldown counter for dodge and take-off (the two contribute different amounts to it)

cooldown.notes: One cooldown for her dodge and her take-off [1]: shared on, a counter in seconds draining a second a second; a dodge adds dash.cooldown, a take-off rise, a landing riseCooldown (the Jet nozzles halve both of the last: config/broom-parts.json). It has room for dash.charges dodges (dash.charges x dash.cooldown seconds; more with Hare's Dash bursts and the Twig bristles): an action goes when the counter is at or under that room less its own amount, so two dodges go straight off and the third waits a second as before, and a landing's 3 s (over the room) means no dodge for 2 s and no rising for 3; after a dodge no take-off for a second. Her trail (trail.cooldown) shows it. Off: the dodge's charges and the rise cooldown run apart as before.

witch.what: Her speeds on the ground and in the treetops, how long rising and descending take, and how the world's lights light her.

decisions.quote: I can go near a coloured light source and not change colour
when you're moving quickly, you jerk up and down with the roll of hills

witch.notes: Speeds per mode, and how long rising and descending take. The witch is lit by the world's lights like everything else [1], but not by her own glow: never darker than lightFloor times her old unlit look, so she reads in the dark; coloured lights (soundsystems, campfires, rune stones, the dancefloor) tint her by lightTint and rim the edge of her facing them by lightRim. Over the hills [2] she and the camera ride a smoothed height, not the ground under her: the ground averaged over heightLookAhead seconds of her flight behind and ahead of her (so the hills' bumps smooth out and she rises early for a crest), eased by heightSmooth seconds at full speed (a damped spring; less as she slows, none standing still; 0 off), and her feet always at least heightClearance metres over the ground under her and a stride ahead.

witch.knock.what: A blow knocks her back and staggers her, harder for big attacks and charges.

decisions.quote: add a knockback and stun on the witch; make it large on chasing/ramming creatures
don't make it stop at scenery

witch.knock.notes: The witch knocked back and staggered by a blow [1]: thrown straight away from the blow, base metres for any blow (bites, swipes, shots) plus scale times the attack's own knockback (combat.json; so a maul, quake or slam sits in between), at least charge metres when it rams her (a charge, or a leap landing on her), at most max; eased off at ease a second (like a creature's knockback), straight through scenery [2], nudged to the nearest clear spot at the end if she'd rest inside a trunk, rock, speaker, soundsystem or the treehouse (the blink's clearances). Staggered (no moving, blinking or 💌s, a wobble and stars) stunBase seconds plus stunScale a metre thrown past base, at most stunMax; then not staggered again for immune seconds (the blows still count), so a pack can't stun-lock her. A blink dodges it all; the blow that knocks her out throws nothing. on false, or ?knock=0, turns it off.

stack.what: The stack of sigils above her hat, swaying like a chain of springs as she moves.

decisions.quote: more opacity, and never obscured by scenery

stack.notes: The sigil stack above the witch's hat: scale (of the sigils' size), offset (the gap between her hat tip and the bottom sigil, in sigil heights), gap (between sigils, in sigil heights). It sways as a chain of springs: stiffness and damping, trail (how far it leans back per m/s of her speed), idleSway (metres of gentle sway when she's still). Its sigils more visible [1]: bright, how bright each stacked sigil is drawn, times leash.sigilGlyph (1 as the sigils on the ground; 1.6 now); backing, a near-black disc behind each (0 none, 1 solid), backSize times the sigil across, so it reads against lit crowns and the sky; over, drawn over the scenery (no depth test, after the see-through pass), so no tree or crown ever hides the stack.

witchHealth.what: The witch [1]: she takes hits (one point each, whatever hits her) before she's knocked out [2]; one comes back every repairTime seconds, the timer starting over whenever she's hit, so to heal she has to get right out of the fight.

decisions.quote: three slashes, and then a final hit

witchHealth.grace.what: seconds after a hit in which no other blow lands, so a pack striking together takes one hit, not all three [1].

witchHealth.slashScale.what: her claw slashes' size relative to her [1].

decisions.quote: the slashes should be twice as large
decisions.rest: render/leash/bubbles.ts; 1 the drawing at her art pixel:, 2

witchHealth.slashGlow.what: their glow, the berries' light drawn in the scene along each stroke so the bloom takes it [1].

decisions.quote: The slashes should glow brighter as well - similar to the berries

knockout.what: What happens when she's knocked out: her creatures go free, she comes back at the treehouse after a wait that grows with each knockdown, and the beat speeds up.

decisions.rest: Ed's playtest of v4821: no sigil made; its rune at its feet, so she can leash it again

decisions.quote: they should idle near where they were dropped, not walk back to their area
decisions.rest: it idles within dropRadius metres of where it was dropped, dancing if that's a party area, till she leashes it again or the night ends (later that day:); it defends what's round it as any happy one, and counts as its kind there for the legends; before, #87, each sigil was put down where its animal stood, parked; at first each turned neutral and went wild again

decisions.quote: We can remove the extra knockdown time
decisions.rest: then, with each knockdown costing a BPM instead,: step 0 and max 6, so every knockdown waits the flat base and the desk's candles are all white

decisions.quote: the BPM goes up by 1 each time you die
decisions.rest: the DJ is off the decks and the crowd gets restless

knockout.notes: Knocked out [1]: she collapses where she is; her sigil stack lets go from the bottom up, one every releaseEach seconds (releaseMax caps the whole release, 0 no cap; an empty stack waits emptyBeat seconds), each animal turning happy where it stands [2][3]; then she sparkles out and back in behind her decks in the treehouse over teleport seconds. Creatures at sigils she had put down on the ground stay hers. One timeline [4], the whole wait counted from her going down: her hat (if it drops) floats to the ground over hatFloat seconds, the screen dimmed, a sad trumpet; she sparkles out and back in behind her decks (teleport seconds); and she scratches there ("Every time she respawns she could do a bit of scratching to increase the respawn time") for the rest of the wait, at least respawn.minScratch, her army fighting on without her, a countdown over her. The wait ("any more than about six seconds to wait will be frustrating ... make each successive death a bit longer, with a cooldown"): respawn.base seconds, respawn.step more for each knockdown within respawn.cooldown seconds of the last, up to respawn.max [5][6]. releaseEach 0 (Ed): her sigils all drop at once as she goes down, under the hat's float. The beat speeds up [7]: each knockdown adds bpmStep to the party's tempo for the rest of the run (bpmCap, if set, is the most it can add), eased in over beat.knockBeats beats (4, a bar) from the next bar line; the music follows the beat clock, and the wave countdown and the ley line's pulse run that much faster (tempo plus bonus over the wave's own tempo), so the waves come sooner.

knockout.legendsLoyal.what: leashed legends stay with her (false: they're let go too: 'they're too old for this'; only a party legend is ever leashed now, and it's always let go).

knockout.dropHat.what: When knocked out she drops her hat where she fell, and wears none till she goes back and picks it up.

decisions.rest: 'when you are killed, you drop your hat, and there's a direction marker for it, so you can go back and find it'

knockout.dropHat.notes: she drops her hat where she went down and wears none till she stands on it and presses the sigil button (E), which puts it straight back on (never into the stack; on top of a sigil, the hat comes first); a 🎩 pointer shows the way meanwhile. Knocked out again with it still down, nothing more drops. A witch with no hat (the character creator's none) has none of this.

knockout.dim.what: how much the screen dims round her while her hat floats off, from the knockdown to her sparkle away (her spot and the hat left lit); no hat, no dim.

decisions.quote: the rest of the screen darkened

knockout.rise.what: the house (rules/treehouse.ts): back at the magic circle after a knockout, she rises out of its floor over rise seconds [1], then walks to her decks and scratches for the rest of the wait.

decisions.rest: blood rises from the floor and forms her shape

knockout.candleStep.what: one candle for every candleStep seconds of the wait (1 or 0.5), white for the base wait, red for the extra from knockdowns in a row; the red burn first.

decisions.rest: the candles along her desk are a loading bar

dash.what: The dash: on the ground she blinks a short way in the direction she's moving and can't be hit for a moment.

decisions.rest: her steering, on the pad and on keyboard and mouse alike, not the way she's aiming; standing still, the way she's facing

dash.notes: The dash, a blink [1]: on the ground only, she vanishes and reappears distance metres the way she's moving [2] in one step, then cooldown seconds before the next. For gone seconds (a few frames) she isn't drawn and can't be hit; otherwise she's as hittable as ever: it's for slipping out of a shot's path. She lands clear of trees, rocks and ruins, soundsystems, the dancefloor's speakers and the treehouse by clear's metres each, the blink shortened to the furthest clear spot.

dash.buffer.what: a press up to this many seconds before she can blink (still recharging, landing, staggered) waits and blinks the moment she can.

dash.toCursor.what: on, she blinks toward the ground under the cursor (or the way the right stick points), the way she faces when the cursor is within aimDead metres of her, and with nothing to aim by (touch) the way she's steering; off, always the way she's steering.

dash.chain.what: the least time, seconds, from one blink to the next, whatever her charges or the shared cooldown say (it keeps a Double blink's two apart; the legend buffs' blink chain, 0.2, before they were removed).

spells.what: Her two spell slots, a hat and a broom, each holding a spell or none.
spells.notes: Spells [1]: two slots, a hat and a broom, each with a spell or none (the plain ones), the hat's chosen in the creator (or ?hat=), the broom's the set its parts complete [2]. Hats are put down with the sigil button held (rules/hat.ts) and work there (some once when placed, some while they lie there); the Helmet is worn. Broom parts change how she moves or pulls (config/broom-parts.json: the Long, Double blink and Haul brooms are the Curled tip, the Twig bristles and the Canoe hull now); an active set spell is cast with the spell button (R; gamepad circle; touch spell), then recharges.

spells.hats.what: the spell hats she owns, a comma list or * for every one [1].

decisions.rest: only the plain hat is hers at first, every spell hat found one a night, rules/finds.ts; the page sets it from her save, app/hatSave.ts, and ?hats= for one load

spells.parts.what: her broom's parts, a comma list of ids from config/broom-parts.json (the page sets it from her save, localStorage witch.broom, fitted at the Workshop's bay; ?parts= for one load); the bare broom, none, has no spell and no quick take-off [1], and a complete set gives its spell.

spells.bag.what: her bag, a config/wardrobe.json bag item's id or empty for none, whose invites multiply invites.cooldown and invites.range while she carries it (rules/bags.ts).
spells.bag.notes: The page sets it from her look (localStorage witch.genome, chosen at the bags station; ?bag=quick or ?bag=far for one load). The Quick bag (bumbag) throws 💌s faster and shorter, the Far bag (satchel) slower and further; none, the tuning's own.

decisions.quote: We should start with a choice of two bags; faster rate of fire but shorter range, and slower rate of fire but longer range

spells.speed.what: the Speed broom, her speed times mult for duration seconds, then cooldown seconds to recharge.

spells.healing.what: The Healing ring heals her while she stands near it, and the Helmet takes the first blow for her.
spells.healing.notes: the Healing ring, within radius m of it she heals a hit every `every` seconds while hurt. The Helmet: the first blow knocks it off beside her instead of costing a hit; she picks it up (E) to wear it again.

spells.battering.what: the Battering broom's blink stuns every wild and enraged creature within width m of its line for stun s [1].

spells.leyjump.what: the Ley jump broom, cast, puts her at the ley line's pulse; cooldown s.

spells.pound.what: the Ground pound broom [1], cast, rises or lands at once, knocking wild and enraged creatures within radius m back push m, and landing stuns them stun s; cooldown s.

spells.stealth.what: the Stealth broom [1]: creatures don't see her unless she threw a 💌 or put down or picked up something in the last reveal s; ones that went for her keep on while she's within range m, then lose her.

spells.harvest.what: the Harvest hat, put down, grows berries berries in a ring radius m round it [1], at most once every every s (the same ring, moved: uneaten ones move with it).

spells.dowsing.what: the Dowsing hat, put down, points to the nearest relic for time s.

spells.sentry.what: the Sentry hat, lying there, throws a 💌 at the nearest invitable creature within range m every every s (Ed: larger ranges).

spells.slingshot.what: the Slingshot hat catches her 💌s flying within catch m, circling it radius m out, holds them hold s and flings each at the nearest invitable creature within fire m, at most max at once.

spells.gathering.what: the Gathering hat, picked up again, brings every sigil of hers within range m back to her stack (Ed: all sigils in range).

spells.bramble.what: the Bramble hat slows wild and enraged creatures within range m of it (Ed: 30 m).

spells.mine.what: the Mine hat, put down, stuns wild and enraged creatures within range m for stun s, at most once every every s.

spells.lullaby.what: the Lullaby hat, put down, sends wild creatures (not enraged) within range m to sleep for time s, at most once every every s; one wakes when a 💌 lands on it [1].

spells.cyclone.what: The Cyclone hat sweeps nearby wild and enraged creatures round it, lifts them and flings them away.
spells.cyclone.notes: the Cyclone hat [1], on putting it down and every every s while it lies there, catches wild and enraged creatures within radius m, sweeps them round it at spin turns a second for time s, lifting them up to lift m, then flings them fling m outward over flingTime s, stunned stun s after they land; never hers, happy ones or legends, and never hurt.

spells.nursing.what: the Nursing hat heals her own creatures within range m of it, rate of their health a second (0.1: whole again in ten seconds).

trail.what: Her flight trail: a glowing ribbon along her path in the colour of the area she's over.

decisions.quote: more like a fading-out glow, similar to the leylines. Its length relates to her speed: 5 m on the ground and 20 m on the treetops. The glow should be the same as the current area colour

trail.notes: Her flight trail [1]: a ribbon of glow along her path, fading to nothing at its tail, in the colour of the area she's over (eased over colourEase seconds as she crosses into the next). Its length: ground metres at full speed on the ground, treetops metres over the treetops, from none below from (a share of her top speed) to full at top speed along curve (1 straight), growing to a new speed's over grow seconds and shrinking over shrink. One trail, one cooldown [2]: it also runs along her blink when she dodges (the ribbon laid along the blink's line, from where she left to where she lands), and it is at least cooldown metres times the share of the shared cooldown counter in use (full right after a take-off or a landing, half after a dodge with two in hand, draining to nothing as the counter empties), so its length shows the cooldown; bySpeed off leaves only that (no length from her speed).

trail.width.what: metres across on the ground and over the treetops.

trail.fade.what: how it fades along its length (eased out: bright for its first stretch, then thinning to nothing; higher keeps it bright longer), its width tapering with it.

trail.sparks.what: the broom's little amber sparks as well. ?trail=0 hides it.

swoopTrail.what: Rainbow trails the party witches leave as they swoop.

decisions.quote: Party-witch swoops should get the same following glow that you have, but it should be bright and multicoloured.

swoopTrail.notes: The party witches' swoop trails [1]: while one swoops she leaves a ribbon in her trail's look, bright and in rainbow colours, each witch starting at her own hue, the colours running along it (hueSpread turns of the wheel a metre) and shifting over time (hueSpeed turns a second), so a crowd of swoops reads as fireworks over the canopy. width metres across (turned to face the camera, so a climb straight up shows), wider in step with its distance from the camera past near metres (so from the treetops it reads as a streak, not a thread), bright its brightness; it fades in as she lifts off over her first liftFade metres, and each stretch of it fades out life seconds after she passed, so it trails out as she lands. At most slots at once (only while the party is stepped: partyWitches.simRange).
